title: First-time Microlearning Panels for Console Routes
creator: Aisha Gomez
description: Design and prototype a set of compact, contextual microlearning panels that surface on a user's first visit to key Redwood Console routes (Model overview, Deployment detail, Rollouts, Cost summary). Panels must teach one clear concept in 1-3 steps, be dismissible, trackable, and safe for A/B testing. The goal is to reduce support questions about basic workflows and increase self-serve activation for first-time users without adding UI clutter for returning users.
acceptance_criteria: Microlearning panels appear only on first visit per route (persisted in user settings) and can be dismissed permanently or snoozed for 24h
Each panel contains a short headline, 1-3 micro-steps with inline visuals, and a single primary CTA (try a quick action) plus a secondary ‘learn more’ link to docs
Panels are responsive and render correctly on desktop and tablet widths used by Console (>= 768px), with accessible contrast and keyboard focus order
Instrumentation emits events: console.microlearn.shown, .clicked_cta, .dismissed, .snoozed with route and variant metadata
Prototype and copy validated in 5 usability sessions with non-Console users; recommended variant has >80% comprehension on the primary task
Design spec and dev handoff document (Figma + dev notes) posted and linked in this ticket
A/B experiment config drafted with success metrics: 10% lift in first-run CTA conversion or 20% reduction in quick-start support clicks
decisions: Use a slide-over micro-panel anchored to top-right of main content area to avoid obscuring primary actions
Limit content to 3 steps with optional inline visual; do not use full-screen modals
Persist dismissal state in user preferences (server-side) to support multi-device consistency
Include analytics context fields: route, variant, user_segment (trial|paid|internal)
Default variant uses inline 'Try it' CTA that triggers a one-click sample operation (eg. run a short inference request) with safe defaults
tasks: Create interactive prototype and record 5 usability sessions (Design / UX Research)
Dev spec: accessibility guidelines, animation timings, instrumentation (Design -> Eng)
Implement front-end components and server-side dismissal persistence (Eng)
Integrate analytics events and A/B experiment flags (Eng / Analytics)
QA pass for responsive layouts and keyboard navigation (QA)
Rollout plan: gradual release to 10% then 50% then 100% (Product)
Monitor metrics for 2 weeks and report on success criteria (Product / Analytics)
notes: Trade-offs: lightweight micro-panels are less discoverable than a full walkthrough but are lower friction for repeated use
Constraint: must not increase initial page load beyond 50ms measured on console entry path — prefer CSS-only animations where possible
Internationalization: copy must be reviewed for key languages; design should accommodate 30% longer translated strings
Accessibility: ensure announcements via ARIA live region when panel appears and that dismiss button is reachable via keyboard
